559	// postBrainArtifacts POSTs the bundle to the hosted brain publish endpoint and
560	// maps the response to a clear error or result. It is the only network call in
561	// the command; it runs only after both opt-in gates have passed.
562	func postBrainArtifacts(ctx context.Context, baseURL, repoID, token string, body publishRequestBody) (publishResult, error) {
563		baseURL, err := apiurl.Validate(baseURL)
564		if err != nil {
565			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
566		}
567		payload, err := json.Marshal(body)
568		if err != nil {
569			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: encode request: %w", err)
570		}
571		// The chokepoint check, not a duplicate of the one in runPublish: this is the
572		// only function that turns a repo id into a network target, and it is reachable
573		// from tests and any future caller that did not come through the command. An id
574		// that is not one bare path segment re-addresses the request — url.PathEscape
575		// cannot prevent that, since "." and ".." are unreserved and survive escaping, so
576		// ".." here yields /api/v1/repos/../brain/artifacts, which normalizes to
577		// /api/v1/brain/artifacts with the caller's bearer token and the whole brain
578		// bundle attached. Refuse before http.NewRequest exists.
579		if err := repoid.Validate(repoID); err != nil {
580			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
581		}
582		// Validated ids equal their own escaped form, so the id is concatenated raw.
583		endpoint := strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/") + publishAPIPathPrefix + repoID + publishAPIPathSuffix
584	
585		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, endpoint, bytes.NewReader(payload))
586		if err != nil {
587			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: build request: %w", err)
588		}
589		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
590		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
591	
592		resp, err := apiurl.WithoutRedirects(publishHTTPClient()).Do(req)
593		if err != nil {
594			// The wrapped error is a *url.Error, whose own Error() renders the target
595			// through url.URL.Redacted() — any userinfo password is printed as "xxxxx".
596			// Interpolating `endpoint` here as well undid exactly that redaction and
597			// printed the cleartext credential. apiurl.Validate now refuses a base URL
598			// carrying userinfo at all, so this is the second of two guards; the target
599			// is still named, by the half of the message that redacts it.
600			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: request failed: %w", err)
601		}
602		defer resp.Body.Close()
603		respBody, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxPublishResponseBytes))
604	
605		switch resp.StatusCode {
606		case http.StatusOK:
607			var result publishResult
608			if err := json.Unmarshal(respBody, &result); err != nil {
609				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: decode server response: %w", err)
610			}
611			// A 200 whose body acknowledges NOTHING is not a success, and reporting it as
612			// one is the worst outcome on this path: the member is told the brain is
613			// published, stops thinking about it, and the hosted brain holds nothing. The
614			// endpoint answers with the coordinate of every artifact it stored, so an
615			// empty `stored` against a non-empty upload means the bytes did not land —
616			// a half-deployed server, a proxy answering `{}` in front of it, or a
617			// response that never came from the endpoint at all. Refuse, and say which
618			// of the two it is rather than guessing on the member's behalf.
619			if len(body.Artifacts) > 0 && len(result.Stored) == 0 {
620				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unacknowledged: the server answered HTTP 200 but acknowledged storing 0 of the %d artifact(s) sent%s; the brain was NOT published — check that %s is the hosted Entire API and not a proxy in front of it",
621					len(body.Artifacts), publishStatusDetail(result.Status, token), endpoint)
622			}
623			// Stored coordinates must cover exactly the submitted set, once each.
624			expected := make(map[[2]string]bool, len(body.Artifacts))
625			for _, artifact := range body.Artifacts {
626				expected[[2]string{artifact.Kind, artifact.Ref}] = true
627			}
628			complete := len(result.Stored) == len(body.Artifacts)
629			for _, stored := range result.Stored {
630				key := [2]string{stored.Kind, stored.Ref}
631				if !expected[key] {
632					complete = false
633				}
634				delete(expected, key)
635			}
636			if !complete || len(expected) != 0 {
637				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unacknowledged: the server did not acknowledge every submitted artifact exactly once%s; check the hosted publish response before retrying", publishStatusDetail(result.Status, token))
638			}
639			return result, nil
640		case http.StatusUnauthorized, http.StatusForbidden:
641			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_auth: authentication or push authorization failed (HTTP %d)%s", resp.StatusCode, publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
642		case http.StatusUnprocessableEntity:
643			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_rejected: server rejected the brain artifacts (HTTP 422)%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
644		case http.StatusServiceUnavailable:
645			// The server uses 503 for more than one reason (no hosted brain on this
646			// deployment, publishing disabled for this jurisdiction, a store that is
647			// temporarily read-only), so its own sentence is the only thing that says
648			// WHICH — dropping the body here left the client guessing on the member's
649			// behalf.
650			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unavailable: hosted brain publishing is not available on the server (HTTP 503)%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
651		case http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge:
652			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_too_large: the server rejected the brain bundle as too large (HTTP 413); its request body exceeds the hosted publish size limit%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
653		default:
654			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_failed: unexpected server response (HTTP %d)%s", resp.StatusCode, publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
655		}
656	}

658	// publishStatusDetail renders the server's own `status` field for the
659	// acknowledged-nothing refusal, as " (status \"...\")", or "" when it said nothing.
660	// It goes through the same terminal-safety cleaning as every other server string
661	// this command prints.
662	func publishStatusDetail(status, token string) string {
663		cleaned := httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorDetailFromBody([]byte(status)), token)
664		if cleaned == "" {
665			return ""
666		}
667		return " (status " + strconv.Quote(cleaned) + ")"
668	}
669	
670	// publishServerDetail renders a short human-readable reason from a server error body.
671	//
672	// It delegates to httpx, which is the shared renderer for every hosted-API error body
673	// in this repo. The local version this replaced handled the ONE shape the endpoint
674	// documents — huma's {"title","detail"} — and pasted everything else through as a
675	// raw 200-byte prefix. That is exactly the wrong answer for the two shapes that
676	// actually show up when the endpoint is not the thing answering: a proxy's HTML page
677	// (200 bytes of doctype and markup, with the useful part — its <title> — usually past
678	// the cut) and a body carrying control bytes, printed straight into the member's
679	// terminal. httpx renders both, and still prefers the envelope's own detail when the
680	// endpoint did answer.
681	//
682	// Every message this suffixes already prints the status ("(HTTP 404)"), so a body
683	// that merely echoes the status text would render doubled: "unexpected server
684	// response (HTTP 404): not found". The echo is stripped; a body saying more keeps
685	// the part beyond it.
686	func publishServerDetail(body []byte, statusCode int, token string) string {
687		detail := httpx.StripStatusEcho(httpx.ErrorDetailFromBody(body),
688			strconv.Itoa(statusCode)+" "+http.StatusText(statusCode))
689		if detail == "" {
690			return ""
691		}
692		// httpx.Redact strips this request's own bearer token from the rendered line: a
693		// server that echoes the Authorization header back would otherwise put it in the
694		// member's stderr, and from there into a CI log or a pasted bug report.
695		return ": " + httpx.Redact(detail, token)
696	}

698	// contentDigest returns the "sha256:"-prefixed lowercase-hex digest of data, the
699	// exact form the wire contract's ContentRef.Digest and the server's VerifyDigest
700	// expect.
701	func contentDigest(data []byte) string {
702		sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
703		return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
704	}

707		if manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
708			return nil
709		}
710		return manifest.Sources.Semantic

713	// readBrainBlob binds a payload to its brain-relative path, rejecting symlinks
714	// in every component and validating the opened regular-file descriptor. Missing
715	// files remain optional; unsafe files fail the bundle instead of being omitted.
716	func readBrainBlob(brainDir, rel string) ([]byte, bool, error) {
717		f, present, err := brainstore.OpenMemoryStateFileExpected(brainDir, rel, "publish artifact", nil)
718		if err != nil || !present {
719			return nil, false, err
720		}
721		defer f.Close()
722		max := clibase.SemanticSnapshotMaxBytes()
723		path := f.Name()
724		if info, err := f.Stat(); err != nil {
725			return nil, false, err
726		} else if info.Size() > max {
727			return nil, false, &readBoundExceededError{Source: path, Max: max}
728		}
729		data, err := clibase.SafeReadAll(f, max, path)
730		if err != nil {
731			return nil, false, err
732		}
733		return data, true, nil
734	}
735	
736	func subdirNames(entries []os.DirEntry) []string {
737		var names []string
738		for _, entry := range entries {
739			if entry.IsDir() {
740				names = append(names, entry.Name())
741			}
742		}
743		return names
744	}
745	
746	// resolveFactStreamBranch validates a stream and recovers the branch that owns
747	// it. Records from other branches are expected content, not corruption: the
748	// hosted pull rebuilds a branch store from the repo-wide feed
749	// (pullHostedFacts), so after a sync on a feature branch the store also
750	// carries teammates' main facts. The owner is therefore not "the records'
751	// branch" but the branch that re-derives the directory name
752	// (factsBranchRelDir is deterministic: slug plus a hash of the full name).
753	// Candidates are every branch the records name, plus the directory's own slug
754	// for a store holding only pulled foreign records. A directory no candidate
755	// re-derives is refused — publishing it under a guessed branch would corrupt
756	// the artifact coordinate. (Residual gap: a store of only foreign records for
757	// a branch whose name sanitizes lossily, e.g. "evis/x"; such a stream fails
758	// publish until the branch distills or records a fact of its own.)
759	func resolveFactStreamBranch(dir string, data []byte) (string, error) {
760		records, err := factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(data))
761		if err != nil {
762			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid fact stream: %w", err)
763		}
764		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
765		var candidates []string
766		for i, record := range records {
767			branch := strings.TrimSpace(record.Branch)
768			if branch == "" {
769				return "", fmt.Errorf("fact record %d has no branch", i+1)
770			}
771			if _, dup := seen[branch]; !dup {
772				seen[branch] = struct{}{}
773				candidates = append(candidates, branch)
774			}
775		}
776		if len(candidates) == 0 {
777			return "", nil
778		}
779		recordBranches := strings.Join(candidates, ", ")
780		if i := len(dir) - len("-01234567"); i > 0 {
781			candidates = append(candidates, dir[:i])
782		}
783		for _, candidate := range candidates {
784			if filepath.Base(factsBranchRelDir(candidate)) == dir {
785				return candidate, nil
786			}
787		}
788		return "", fmt.Errorf("directory name matches no branch named by its records (%s); refusing to publish the stream under a guessed branch", recordBranches)
789	}
790	
791	// overlayBranchName reads the advisory "branch" field from an overlay payload.
792	func overlayBranchName(data []byte) string {
793		var payload struct {
794			Branch string `json:"branch"`
795		}
796		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &payload); err != nil {
797			return ""
798		}
799		return strings.TrimSpace(payload.Branch)
800	}

32	// Hosted brain publish (P1.M1.5, client half). This command is the ONLY path in
33	// the plugin allowed to egress brain data, and only behind an explicit opt-in.

35	// No implicit egress (ADR-P1-A, amended by COR-2111): a network call happens
36	// only when the user explicitly runs `entire brain publish` AND supplies the
37	// full target (repo id, API URL, token) — there are no target defaults, so a
38	// bare invocation refuses BEFORE any resolution, disk read, or HTTP request.
39	// The ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_HOSTED env gate this command originally required was
40	// retired once `entire brain connect` made hosted consent an explicit, durable
41	// state. The master kill switch (ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS) always wins.
42	//
43	// Where the bundle may go is gated too: the resolved base URL must clear the shared
44	// scheme floor (internal/apiurl) — https, or http only to a loopback host — checked
45	// on the same egress-free side of the disk read as the two gates above, so an
46	// unsafe or malformed target never gets the brain built for it.
47	const (
48		// The hosted target is resolved from these env vars (each overridable by a
49		// flag). There is no pre-existing entire-api client in this plugin, so these
50		// follow the plugin's ENTIRE_* environment convention. Auth is a bearer token,
51		// matching the entire-api brain publish endpoint's push gate.
52		envAPIBaseURL = "ENTIRE_API_URL"
53		envAPIToken   = "REDACTED"

57	const (
58		// Artifact kinds, matching the server's brainstore.Kind* constants exactly.
59		brainKindSnapshot = "snapshot"
60		brainKindOverlay  = "overlay"
61		brainKindFacts    = "facts"
62		brainKindManifest = "manifest"
63	
64		mediaTypeJSON   = "application/json"
65		mediaTypeNDJSON = "application/x-ndjson"

67		// publishAPIPath is the route on entire-api: POST
68		// {base}/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/artifacts.
69		publishAPIPathPrefix = "/api/v1/repos/"
70		publishAPIPathSuffix = "/brain/artifacts"
71	
72		publishRequestTimeout   = 5 * time.Minute
73		maxPublishResponseBytes = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB is ample for the small JSON result.
74	
75		// serverMaxBrainBodyBytes mirrors entire-api's maxBrainArtifactBytes: the
76		// publish endpoint caps the request body at 256 MiB and 413s anything larger (a
77		// brain bundle inlines all its blobs as base64 in one JSON body). The client
78		// preflights against this so an oversized bundle fails locally with a precise
79		// message before a multi-GB buffer is ever built.
80		serverMaxBrainBodyBytes = 256 << 20 // 256 MiB
81	
82		// publishBodyHeadroom keeps the client ceiling below the server cap so the
83		// projection's rounding can never let through a body the server would 413.
84		publishBodyHeadroom = 8 << 20 // 8 MiB

86		// publishArtifactEnvelopeBytes over-estimates one artifact's JSON structural
87		// overhead ({"kind":..,"ref":..,"digest":..,"data":..}) so the projected body
88		// size stays an upper bound on the real marshaled body.

136			Long: `Publish serializes the current on-disk brain into the versioned brain wire
137	artifacts (manifest, branch overlays, and durable facts) and
138	uploads them to hosted Entire.
139	
140	Hosted publishing is opt-in and off by default: the brain stays entirely local
141	unless you run this command with a target — the connected binding by default
142	(see 'entire brain connect'), or an explicit one. No brain data ever leaves
143	your machine implicitly, and ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS always wins.
144	
145	The target repo, API base URL, and bearer token resolve flag > env > connected
146	binding: --repo-id / ENTIRE_REPO_ID, --api-url / ENTIRE_API_URL, --token /
147	ENTIRE_API_TOKEN. On a connected repo the token is minted via the host CLI. The

151	Re-running publish is safe: the server overwrites each artifact at its
152	coordinate, so identical bytes produce an identical result.`,

155				return runPublish(cmd.Context(), cmd, opts, publishOpts)

160		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&publishOpts.apiURL, "api-url", "", "Entire API base URL, https:// (overrides ENTIRE_API_URL)")

166	func runPublish(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, publishOpts publishCommandOptions) error {
167		// Every gate is checked BEFORE resolving any target, reading the brain, or
168		// making a network call, so a refusal is guaranteed egress-free.
169	
170		// The master kill switch always wins over the hosted opt-in.
171		if clibase.BrainNoEgressMode() {
172			return fmt.Errorf("no_egress: hosted brain publish is disabled while %s is set; unset it to publish", clibase.NoEgressToggleName())
173		}
174	
175		// Locate the on-disk brain for this repo; the connected binding under it is
176		// the default target.
177		repoDir := opts.Env.RepoRoot
178		if repoDir == "" {
179			repoDir = "."
180		}
181		storage, err := repoStoragePaths(ctx, opts.Runner, opts.Env, repoDir)
182		if err != nil {
183			return fmt.Errorf("publish: resolve brain: %w", err)
184		}
185	
186		// Resolve the target: flag > env > connected binding. Validation (repo-id
187		// path segment, URL scheme floor) happens inside, before any brain read or
188		// network call, so a malformed or missing target refuses with the whole
189		// brain still on disk — the same egress-free guarantee as the gate above.
190		target, err := resolveManualHostedTarget(ctx, opts, storage.BrainDir, repoDir, "publish", publishOpts.repoID, publishOpts.apiURL, publishOpts.token)
191		if err != nil {
192			return err
193		}
194		repoID, baseURL, token := target.repoID, target.baseURL, target.token
195		if !brainExportExists(storage.BrainDir) {
196			return errors.New("publish: no brain found for this repo; run '" + clibase.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "' first")
197		}
198	
199		// Exclusion and purge use the same boundary. Hold it from collection through
200		// the completed HTTP exchange so a checked bundle cannot become private
201		// between its policy read and its last outgoing byte.
202		privacyUnlock, err := brainstore.AcquireBrainPrivacySideEffectLock(storage.BrainDir)
203		if err != nil {
204			return fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
205		}
206		defer privacyUnlock()
207	
208		body, repoKey, err := buildPublishBundle(ctx, opts, storage, repoDir)
209		if err != nil {
210			return fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
211		}
212	
213		result, err := postBrainArtifacts(ctx, baseURL, repoID, token, body)
214		if err != nil {
215			return err
216		}
217	
218		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "published %d artifact(s) for %s to %s\n",
219			len(result.Stored), repoKey, strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/"))
220		return nil
221	}
222	
223	// publishFlagOrEnv returns the trimmed flag value when set, else the trimmed
224	// environment value.
225	func publishFlagOrEnv(flagVal, envName string) string {
226		if v := strings.TrimSpace(flagVal); v != "" {
227			return v
228		}
229		return strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(envName))
230	}
231	
232	// buildPublishBundle serializes the on-disk brain into the publish bundle: the
233	// manifest (kind=manifest, its data is the full brainwire.BrainArtifact JSON with
234	// content-addressed references) plus each snapshot/overlay/facts blob inline. It
235	// returns the bundle and the repo_key it declares.
236	func buildPublishBundle(ctx context.Context, opts Options, storage repoStorage, repoDir string) (publishRequestBody, string, error) {
237		manifest, err := loadBrainManifest(storage.BrainDir)
238		if err != nil {
239			return publishRequestBody{}, "", fmt.Errorf("load brain manifest: %w", err)
240		}
241		// The wire manifest's repo_key MUST equal the slug entire-api resolves the
242		// target repo_id to server-side ("gh/owner/repo"), or the server 422s the whole
243		// bundle. Derive it from the origin remote in that canonical form rather than
244		// forwarding the on-disk store key (whose per-host DomainSlugs prefix the
245		// GitHub-sourced server can never reproduce). The on-disk RepoKey stays the
246		// local store's identity and is intentionally not sent as the wire key.
247		repoKey, err := canonicalWireRepoKey(ctx, opts, repoDir)
248		if err != nil {
249			return publishRequestBody{}, "", err
250		}
251	
252		art := brainwire.NewBrainArtifact(repoKey, manifest.DefaultBranch, manifest.GeneratedAt)
253		if sem := semanticSourceOf(manifest); sem != nil {
254			art.SetProvider(sem.Provider, sem.ProviderVersion, sem.SchemaVersion)
255		}
256	
257		// Collect the heavy blobs (each also registers a content-addressed reference on
258		// the wire manifest). Order within each kind is stable so re-publishing an
259		// unchanged brain produces a byte-identical request (idempotent).
260		var blobs []publishArtifact
261		overlays, err := collectOverlayArtifacts(art, storage.BrainDir)
262		if err != nil {
263			return publishRequestBody{}, "", err
264		}
265		blobs = append(blobs, overlays...)
266		facts, err := collectFactArtifacts(art, storage.BrainDir)
267		if err != nil {
268			return publishRequestBody{}, "", err
269		}
270		blobs = append(blobs, facts...)
271	
272		// The manifest artifact is the fully-built wire artifact (manifest header +
273		// all references), addressed by the repo's HEAD commit (the store addresses a
274		// manifest by commit).
275		manifestData, err := json.Marshal(art)
276		if err != nil {
277			return publishRequestBody{}, "", fmt.Errorf("encode manifest: %w", err)
278		}
279		manifestArtifact := publishArtifact{
280			Kind:   brainKindManifest,
281			Ref:    publishManifestRef(ctx, opts, repoDir, manifest),
282			Digest: contentDigest(manifestData),
283			Data:   manifestData,
284		}
285	
286		body := publishRequestBody{
287			Artifacts: append([]publishArtifact{manifestArtifact}, blobs...),
288		}
289		// Preflight the total bundle size against the server's 256 MiB body cap BEFORE
290		// json.Marshal base64-expands every blob into one buffer, so an oversized brain
291		// fails with a precise local message instead of building a multi-GB body only to
292		// be 413'd with an opaque error.
293		if err := ensurePublishBodyWithinLimit(body); err != nil {
294			return publishRequestBody{}, "", err
295		}
296		return body, repoKey, nil
297	}
298	
299	// brainProviderPrefixGitHub is the wire-contract domain slug for github.com
300	// (entire-brain's knownRepoDomainSlugs maps github.com -> "gh"). entire-api's
301	// brain store is GitHub-sourced, so its server-side slug resolver ALWAYS renders a
302	// repo as "gh/owner/repo" from the stored github.com full name — it never sees the
303	// client's per-host DomainSlugs. Only a github.com remote can therefore produce a
304	// wire repo_key the server accepts.
305	const brainProviderPrefixGitHub = "gh"
306	
307	// canonicalWireRepoKey derives the wire manifest repo_key from the repo's origin
308	// remote in the exact form entire-api's brainSlugResolver emits:
309	// "gh/" + <normalized owner>/<normalized repo>. Owner/repo come from the same
310	// parseRepoRemote the on-disk store key uses (each component lowercased and run
311	// through safeRepoPathComponent — byte-identical to the server's wireRepoPath).
312	//
313	// Only a github.com origin is accepted: entire-api's brain store is sourced from
314	// github_repo_meta (github.com repos) and its resolver UNCONDITIONALLY renders
315	// "gh/owner/repo" from the stored full name — it has no notion of the client's git
316	// host, so it can never reproduce a slug for a GitHub Enterprise or look-alike
317	// "github.*" host. Admitting those would send a key the server 422s (or, on an
318	// owner/repo collision with a user-supplied github.com repo_id, overwrite the wrong
319	// repo's brain), so any non-github.com host fails fast here. github.com's own
320	// naming rules forbid an owner or repo that is all punctuation, so every valid
321	// github.com full name normalizes to two non-empty components and matches the
322	// server's empty-preserving join exactly.
323	func canonicalWireRepoKey(ctx context.Context, opts Options, repoDir string) (string, error) {
324		remote := strings.TrimSpace(string(runGitOutput(ctx, opts.Runner, repoDir, "remote", "get-url", "origin")))
325		host, components, ok := parseRepoRemote(remote)
326		if !ok {
327			return "", fmt.Errorf("could not resolve a git origin remote for this repo; hosted publish requires a github.com origin remote")
328		}
329		if !isGitHubDotComHost(host) {
330			return "", fmt.Errorf("hosted publish currently supports github.com-hosted repos only; origin remote host %q is not github.com (the hosted brain store is GitHub-sourced)", host)
331		}
332		return brainProviderPrefixGitHub + "/" + strings.Join(components, "/"), nil
333	}
334	
335	// isGitHubDotComHost reports whether host is exactly github.com — the only host
336	// whose repos entire-api's GitHub-sourced resolver serves under the "gh" provider
337	// prefix. GitHub Enterprise / self-hosted / look-alike "github.*" hosts are NOT
338	// accepted: the public github.com-sourced server cannot resolve them, so a wire key
339	// for such a host would 422 (or collide with an unrelated github.com repo).
340	func isGitHubDotComHost(host string) bool {
341		return normalizeRepoHost(host) == "github.com"
342	}
343	
344	// ensurePublishBodyWithinLimit refuses a bundle whose projected request body would
345	// exceed the hosted publish size ceiling, BEFORE json.Marshal builds the
346	// base64-expanded body in memory. The error names the projected size and the limit
347	// so the failure is actionable rather than an opaque server 413.
348	func ensurePublishBodyWithinLimit(body publishRequestBody) error {
349		if projected := projectedPublishBodyBytes(body); projected > maxPublishBodyBytes {
350			return fmt.Errorf("publish_too_large: the brain bundle is ~%d bytes, over the %d-byte hosted publish limit; refresh a smaller brain or publish fewer artifacts", projected, maxPublishBodyBytes)
351		}
352		return nil
353	}
354	
355	// projectedPublishBodyBytes upper-bounds the size of the marshaled JSON request
356	// body without marshaling it: each artifact's Data becomes base64 (4/3 expansion,
357	// rounded up) plus a generous fixed JSON envelope, summed with the array framing.
358	// It never undershoots the real body, so a bundle that clears this check also
359	// clears the server's body cap.
360	func projectedPublishBodyBytes(body publishRequestBody) int64 {
361		total := int64(len(`{"artifacts":[]}`))
362		for i, a := range body.Artifacts {
363			if i > 0 {
364				total++ // comma between array elements
365			}
366			total += publishArtifactEnvelopeBytes
367			total += int64(len(a.Kind) + len(a.Ref) + len(a.Digest))
368			total += int64(base64.StdEncoding.EncodedLen(len(a.Data)))
369		}
370		return total
371	}
372	
373	// collectOverlayArtifacts reads semantic/overlays/<base>..<head>.json, keying
374	// each by "base..head", and registers an OverlayRef on art. The all-branches.json
375	// refresh report is not a (base,head) overlay and is skipped.
376	func collectOverlayArtifacts(art *brainwire.BrainArtifact, brainDir string) ([]publishArtifact, error) {
377		entries, _, err := brainstore.ReadPrivacyDirectory(brainDir, filepath.Join(semanticDirName, "overlays"), "publish overlays")
378		if err != nil {
379			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
380				return nil, nil
381			}

425	// collectFactArtifacts reads facts/<slug>/facts.ndjson, recovering each stream's
426	// logical branch (resolveFactStreamBranch), and registers a FactsRef on art.
427	// Streams are keyed by branch and emitted in branch order.
428	func collectFactArtifacts(art *brainwire.BrainArtifact, brainDir string) ([]publishArtifact, error) {
429		manifest, err := loadBrainManifest(brainDir)
430		if err != nil {
431			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load facts privacy manifest: %w", err)
432		}
433		guard, err := loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)
434		if err != nil {
435			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load facts privacy policy: %w", err)
436		}
437		entries, _, err := brainstore.ReadPrivacyDirectory(brainDir, factsDirName, "publish facts")
438		if err != nil {
439			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
440				return nil, nil
441			}
442			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts: %w", err)
443		}

445		dirs := subdirNames(entries)
446		sort.Strings(dirs)
447	
448		type factStream struct {
449			branch string
450			data   []byte
451		}
452		var streams []factStream
453		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
454		for _, dir := range dirs {
455			data, ok, err := readBrainBlob(brainDir, filepath.Join(factsDirName, dir, factsFileName))
456			if err != nil {
457				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: %w", dir, err)
458			}
459			if !ok {
460				continue
461			}
462			branch, err := resolveFactStreamBranch(dir, data)
463			if err != nil {
464				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: %w", dir, err)
465			}
466			if branch == "" {
467				continue
468			}
469			if _, dup := seen[branch]; dup {
470				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: duplicate branch stream %q", dir, branch)
471			}
472			seen[branch] = struct{}{}
473			streams = append(streams, factStream{branch: branch, data: data})
474		}
475		sort.Slice(streams, func(i, j int) bool { return streams[i].branch < streams[j].branch })
476	
477		var out []publishArtifact
478		for _, stream := range streams {
479			// REDACT before the bytes become an artifact. The digest and the manifest
480			// ContentRef must describe what actually leaves, so the redaction has to
481			// happen ahead of both.
482			data, err := redactFactsForEgress(stream.data, guard)
483			if err != nil {
484				return nil, fmt.Errorf("read facts %s: %w", stream.branch, err)
485			}

487			digest := contentDigest(data)
488			art.AddFacts(brainwire.FactsRef{
489				Branch:  stream.branch,
490				Content: brainwire.ContentRef{Digest: digest, Size: int64(len(data)), MediaType: mediaTypeNDJSON, Path: rel},
491			})
492			out = append(out, publishArtifact{Kind: brainKindFacts, Ref: stream.branch, Digest: digest, Data: data})
493		}
494		return out, nil
495	}

497	// redactFactsForEgress re-renders a facts stream with the LOCAL-ONLY provenance
498	// coordinates stripped, which is what `facts sync` has always done and what publish
499	// did not.
500	//
501	// A distilled fact's anchor mixes two kinds of value (see factsync.SanitizeForEgress):
502	// opaque cross-member ids another member can carry but never resolve (session id,
503	// commit, checkpoint, turn), and the coordinates of a private file on THIS machine —
504	// Transcript, a brain-relative transcript path, and Line, a turn offset into it. The
505	// path is not an opaque handle: it is rendered as
506	//
507	//	sessions/main/20260530T174906Z_codex_<session-uuid>_<checkpoint>.jsonl
508	//
509	// so shipping it hands the other side a dated inventory of the member's private
510	// sessions — when each ran, which agent tool ran it — and, with Line, the exact turn
511	// a statement came from. None of it is needed to consume a fact: the reasoning layer
512	// treats a peer's anchor as opaque and never resolves one (ADR-P1).
513	//
514	// factsync.SanitizeForEgress is the SAME redaction the fact-set sync and the
515	// proposal push apply, deliberately rather than a second copy of the rule: the two
516	// egress paths carry the same records to the same service, so they must agree on
517	// what may leave, and one implementation is how that stays true.
518	//
519	// A stream that will not parse is an ERROR, not a stream to ship unredacted. It is
520	// also not a new class of failure: `facts sync` already refuses the same file, so a
521	// brain that cannot publish here could not sync either.
522	func redactFactsForEgress(data []byte, guard sessionReadGuard) ([]byte, error) {
523		records, err := factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(data))
524		if err != nil {
525			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot redact local-only provenance before upload: %w", err)
526		}
527		// Filter before sanitizing: transcript coordinates are needed to recognize
528		// excluded provenance when an anchor has no session ID.
529		records = guardFactRecords(guard, records)
530		var buf bytes.Buffer
531		if err := factmerge.WriteNDJSON(&buf, factsync.SanitizeForEgress(records)); err != nil {
532			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot redact local-only provenance before upload: %w", err)
533		}
534		return buf.Bytes(), nil
535	}

552	// publishHTTPClient retains dial/TLS bounds and the full five-minute budget for
553	// uploading and processing a bundle. It shares the upload connection pool, whose
554	// header bound permits server processing after a large request has been sent.
555	func publishHTTPClient() *http.Client {
556		return httpx.UploadClient(publishRequestTimeout)
557	}

559	// postBrainArtifacts POSTs the bundle to the hosted brain publish endpoint and
560	// maps the response to a clear error or result. It is the only network call in
561	// the command; it runs only after both opt-in gates have passed.
562	func postBrainArtifacts(ctx context.Context, baseURL, repoID, token string, body publishRequestBody) (publishResult, error) {
563		baseURL, err := apiurl.Validate(baseURL)
564		if err != nil {
565			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
566		}
567		payload, err := json.Marshal(body)
568		if err != nil {
569			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: encode request: %w", err)
570		}
571		// The chokepoint check, not a duplicate of the one in runPublish: this is the
572		// only function that turns a repo id into a network target, and it is reachable
573		// from tests and any future caller that did not come through the command. An id
574		// that is not one bare path segment re-addresses the request — url.PathEscape
575		// cannot prevent that, since "." and ".." are unreserved and survive escaping, so
576		// ".." here yields /api/v1/repos/../brain/artifacts, which normalizes to
577		// /api/v1/brain/artifacts with the caller's bearer token and the whole brain
578		// bundle attached. Refuse before http.NewRequest exists.
579		if err := repoid.Validate(repoID); err != nil {
580			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: %w", err)
581		}
582		// Validated ids equal their own escaped form, so the id is concatenated raw.
583		endpoint := strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/") + publishAPIPathPrefix + repoID + publishAPIPathSuffix
584	
585		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, endpoint, bytes.NewReader(payload))
586		if err != nil {
587			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: build request: %w", err)
588		}
589		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
590		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
591	
592		resp, err := apiurl.WithoutRedirects(publishHTTPClient()).Do(req)
593		if err != nil {
594			// The wrapped error is a *url.Error, whose own Error() renders the target
595			// through url.URL.Redacted() — any userinfo password is printed as "xxxxx".
596			// Interpolating `endpoint` here as well undid exactly that redaction and
597			// printed the cleartext credential. apiurl.Validate now refuses a base URL
598			// carrying userinfo at all, so this is the second of two guards; the target
599			// is still named, by the half of the message that redacts it.
600			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: request failed: %w", err)
601		}
602		defer resp.Body.Close()
603		respBody, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxPublishResponseBytes))
604	
605		switch resp.StatusCode {
606		case http.StatusOK:
607			var result publishResult
608			if err := json.Unmarshal(respBody, &result); err != nil {
609				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish: decode server response: %w", err)
610			}
611			// A 200 whose body acknowledges NOTHING is not a success, and reporting it as
612			// one is the worst outcome on this path: the member is told the brain is
613			// published, stops thinking about it, and the hosted brain holds nothing. The
614			// endpoint answers with the coordinate of every artifact it stored, so an
615			// empty `stored` against a non-empty upload means the bytes did not land —
616			// a half-deployed server, a proxy answering `{}` in front of it, or a
617			// response that never came from the endpoint at all. Refuse, and say which
618			// of the two it is rather than guessing on the member's behalf.
619			if len(body.Artifacts) > 0 && len(result.Stored) == 0 {
620				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unacknowledged: the server answered HTTP 200 but acknowledged storing 0 of the %d artifact(s) sent%s; the brain was NOT published — check that %s is the hosted Entire API and not a proxy in front of it",
621					len(body.Artifacts), publishStatusDetail(result.Status, token), endpoint)
622			}
623			// Stored coordinates must cover exactly the submitted set, once each.
624			expected := make(map[[2]string]bool, len(body.Artifacts))
625			for _, artifact := range body.Artifacts {
626				expected[[2]string{artifact.Kind, artifact.Ref}] = true
627			}
628			complete := len(result.Stored) == len(body.Artifacts)
629			for _, stored := range result.Stored {
630				key := [2]string{stored.Kind, stored.Ref}
631				if !expected[key] {
632					complete = false
633				}
634				delete(expected, key)
635			}
636			if !complete || len(expected) != 0 {
637				return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unacknowledged: the server did not acknowledge every submitted artifact exactly once%s; check the hosted publish response before retrying", publishStatusDetail(result.Status, token))
638			}
639			return result, nil
640		case http.StatusUnauthorized, http.StatusForbidden:
641			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_auth: authentication or push authorization failed (HTTP %d)%s", resp.StatusCode, publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
642		case http.StatusUnprocessableEntity:
643			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_rejected: server rejected the brain artifacts (HTTP 422)%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
644		case http.StatusServiceUnavailable:
645			// The server uses 503 for more than one reason (no hosted brain on this
646			// deployment, publishing disabled for this jurisdiction, a store that is
647			// temporarily read-only), so its own sentence is the only thing that says
648			// WHICH — dropping the body here left the client guessing on the member's
649			// behalf.
650			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_unavailable: hosted brain publishing is not available on the server (HTTP 503)%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
651		case http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge:
652			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_too_large: the server rejected the brain bundle as too large (HTTP 413); its request body exceeds the hosted publish size limit%s", publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
653		default:
654			return publishResult{}, fmt.Errorf("publish_failed: unexpected server response (HTTP %d)%s", resp.StatusCode, publishServerDetail(respBody, resp.StatusCode, token))
655		}
656	}

658	// publishStatusDetail renders the server's own `status` field for the
659	// acknowledged-nothing refusal, as " (status \"...\")", or "" when it said nothing.
660	// It goes through the same terminal-safety cleaning as every other server string
661	// this command prints.
662	func publishStatusDetail(status, token string) string {
663		cleaned := httpx.Redact(httpx.ErrorDetailFromBody([]byte(status)), token)
664		if cleaned == "" {
665			return ""
666		}
667		return " (status " + strconv.Quote(cleaned) + ")"
668	}
669	
670	// publishServerDetail renders a short human-readable reason from a server error body.
671	//
672	// It delegates to httpx, which is the shared renderer for every hosted-API error body
673	// in this repo. The local version this replaced handled the ONE shape the endpoint
674	// documents — huma's {"title","detail"} — and pasted everything else through as a
675	// raw 200-byte prefix. That is exactly the wrong answer for the two shapes that
676	// actually show up when the endpoint is not the thing answering: a proxy's HTML page
677	// (200 bytes of doctype and markup, with the useful part — its <title> — usually past
678	// the cut) and a body carrying control bytes, printed straight into the member's
679	// terminal. httpx renders both, and still prefers the envelope's own detail when the
680	// endpoint did answer.
681	//
682	// Every message this suffixes already prints the status ("(HTTP 404)"), so a body
683	// that merely echoes the status text would render doubled: "unexpected server
684	// response (HTTP 404): not found". The echo is stripped; a body saying more keeps
685	// the part beyond it.
686	func publishServerDetail(body []byte, statusCode int, token string) string {
687		detail := httpx.StripStatusEcho(httpx.ErrorDetailFromBody(body),
688			strconv.Itoa(statusCode)+" "+http.StatusText(statusCode))
689		if detail == "" {
690			return ""
691		}
692		// httpx.Redact strips this request's own bearer token from the rendered line: a
693		// server that echoes the Authorization header back would otherwise put it in the
694		// member's stderr, and from there into a CI log or a pasted bug report.
695		return ": " + httpx.Redact(detail, token)
696	}

698	// contentDigest returns the "sha256:"-prefixed lowercase-hex digest of data, the
699	// exact form the wire contract's ContentRef.Digest and the server's VerifyDigest
700	// expect.
701	func contentDigest(data []byte) string {
702		sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
703		return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
704	}

706	func semanticSourceOf(manifest *exportManifest) *semanticSourceManifest {
707		if manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
708			return nil
709		}
710		return manifest.Sources.Semantic

713	// readBrainBlob binds a payload to its brain-relative path, rejecting symlinks
714	// in every component and validating the opened regular-file descriptor. Missing
715	// files remain optional; unsafe files fail the bundle instead of being omitted.
716	func readBrainBlob(brainDir, rel string) ([]byte, bool, error) {
717		f, present, err := brainstore.OpenMemoryStateFileExpected(brainDir, rel, "publish artifact", nil)
718		if err != nil || !present {
719			return nil, false, err
720		}
721		defer f.Close()
722		max := clibase.SemanticSnapshotMaxBytes()
723		path := f.Name()
724		if info, err := f.Stat(); err != nil {
725			return nil, false, err
726		} else if info.Size() > max {
727			return nil, false, &readBoundExceededError{Source: path, Max: max}
728		}
729		data, err := clibase.SafeReadAll(f, max, path)
730		if err != nil {
731			return nil, false, err
732		}
733		return data, true, nil
734	}

736	func subdirNames(entries []os.DirEntry) []string {
737		var names []string
738		for _, entry := range entries {
739			if entry.IsDir() {
740				names = append(names, entry.Name())
741			}
742		}
743		return names
744	}

746	// resolveFactStreamBranch validates a stream and recovers the branch that owns
747	// it. Records from other branches are expected content, not corruption: the
748	// hosted pull rebuilds a branch store from the repo-wide feed
749	// (pullHostedFacts), so after a sync on a feature branch the store also
750	// carries teammates' main facts. The owner is therefore not "the records'
751	// branch" but the branch that re-derives the directory name
752	// (factsBranchRelDir is deterministic: slug plus a hash of the full name).
753	// Candidates are every branch the records name, plus the directory's own slug
754	// for a store holding only pulled foreign records. A directory no candidate
755	// re-derives is refused — publishing it under a guessed branch would corrupt
756	// the artifact coordinate. (Residual gap: a store of only foreign records for
757	// a branch whose name sanitizes lossily, e.g. "evis/x"; such a stream fails
758	// publish until the branch distills or records a fact of its own.)
759	func resolveFactStreamBranch(dir string, data []byte) (string, error) {
760		records, err := factmerge.ParseNDJSON(bytes.NewReader(data))
761		if err != nil {
762			return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid fact stream: %w", err)
763		}
764		seen := make(map[string]struct{})
765		var candidates []string
766		for i, record := range records {
767			branch := strings.TrimSpace(record.Branch)
768			if branch == "" {
769				return "", fmt.Errorf("fact record %d has no branch", i+1)
770			}
771			if _, dup := seen[branch]; !dup {
772				seen[branch] = struct{}{}
773				candidates = append(candidates, branch)
774			}
775		}
776		if len(candidates) == 0 {
777			return "", nil
778		}
779		recordBranches := strings.Join(candidates, ", ")
780		if i := len(dir) - len("-01234567"); i > 0 {
781			candidates = append(candidates, dir[:i])
782		}
783		for _, candidate := range candidates {
784			if filepath.Base(factsBranchRelDir(candidate)) == dir {
785				return candidate, nil
786			}
787		}
788		return "", fmt.Errorf("directory name matches no branch named by its records (%s); refusing to publish the stream under a guessed branch", recordBranches)
789	}

791	// overlayBranchName reads the advisory "branch" field from an overlay payload.
792	func overlayBranchName(data []byte) string {
793		var payload struct {
794			Branch string `json:"branch"`
795		}
796		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &payload); err != nil {
797			return ""
798		}
799		return strings.TrimSpace(payload.Branch)
800	}

38		PullSucceeded bool
39	}

41	// hostedFactsSyncAndPull closes the hosted-memory loop for one branch on the
42	// per-fact wire (COR-2126): batch-upsert this machine's branch store to
43	// brainstore, pull the repo-wide delta feed into the repo-level cache, and
44	// rebuild the branch store as the pull filter's output plus this machine's
45	// own facts the feed has not seen. No CAS, no branch heads, no proposals —
46	// per-fact storage keeps conflicting facts side by side and resolution stays
47	// deferred to the async pipeline.
48	//
49	// It is a NEVER-FAILS step: every gated or soft failure is one stderr line and
50	// a nil return, because its callers (daemon tick, session-end hook, connect)
51	// must not fail on hosted outages. The error return exists for programming
52	// errors only.
53	//
54	// Gate order is fixed: (1) the local-only kill switch always wins; (2) a
55	// recorded opt-out (`entire brain disconnect`) stops sync until `connect`
56	// clears it; (3) the repo binding is the consent AND the connection state —
57	// only `entire brain connect` (or the future onboarding flow) writes it, so an
58	// absent binding means local-only, silently, every run. Background triggers
59	// never connect a repo. (4) apiurl.Validate before any client exists. A fresh
60	// token is minted per call via the host CLI's own login and held only in
61	// memory.
62	//
63	// The outcome reports what actually happened: Attempted is whether the gates
64	// passed and the server was contacted (callers that log success must not
65	// report a gated no-op as a sync that ran); PullSucceeded is whether the pull
66	// half completed — the half that proves the exchange (the per-branch marker
67	// keys off it). Callers that promise a sync to the user (connect) key their
68	// report off PullSucceeded; background callers keep ignoring it.
69	func hostedFactsSyncAndPull(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, opts Options, repoDir string, storage repoStorage, branch string) (hostedSyncOutcome, error) {
70		if base.BrainNoEgressMode() {
71			return hostedSyncOutcome{}, nil
72		}
73		binding, present, err := readHostedRepoBinding(storage.BrainDir)
74		if err != nil {

76			// hide a recorded opt-out (privacy) or a custom target, and neither
77			// survives a rewrite. Skip loudly; the remedy is an explicit
78			// `entire brain connect`.
79			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: skipped: %v\n", err)
80			return hostedSyncOutcome{}, nil
81		}
82		if !present || binding.OptedOut {
83			return hostedSyncOutcome{}, nil
84		}
85		baseURL, err := apiurl.Validate(binding.BaseURL)

88			return hostedSyncOutcome{}, nil
89		}
90		token, err := mintHostedToken(ctx, opts.Runner, repoDir, hostEntireBinary)
91		if err != nil {

94		}
95		srv := &factsync.HTTPServer{BaseURL: baseURL, Token: token}
96	
97		counts, skipped, pushErr := pushHostedFacts(ctx, storage, srv, binding.RepoID, branch)
98		if skipped > 0 {
99			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: branch %s: skipped %d unpublishable record(s) whose content id does not re-derive (kept locally, not uploaded)\n", branch, skipped)
100		}
101		pushed := pushErr == nil
102		if pushErr != nil {
103			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: branch %s publish failed (local brain unaffected): %v; pull-only\n", branch, pushErr)
104		}
105		kept, total, manifestErr, pullErr := pullHostedFacts(ctx, opts, repoDir, storage, srv, binding.RepoID, baseURL, token, branch)
106		if pullErr != nil {
107			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: branch %s pull failed (local brain unaffected): %v\n", branch, pullErr)
108			return hostedSyncOutcome{Attempted: true}, nil
109		}
110		if pushed {
111			// The per-branch marker records that this branch completed a sync
112			// against this target; the blind-spot note keys off its absence. It
113			// needs BOTH halves: a pull-only run leaves it unwritten, and so does
114			// a failed pull — the empty-store push "succeeds" without contacting
115			// the server, so the pull is what proves the exchange happened.
116			if err := writeHostedFactsBinding(storage.BrainDir, branch, binding.RepoID, baseURL); err != nil {
117				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: record hosted target: %v\n", err)
118			}
119		}
120		if manifestErr != nil {
121			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: facts updated, but the source manifest could not be refreshed: %v\n", manifestErr)
122		}
123		fmt.Fprintf(errW, "hosted sync: branch %s pushed added=%d changed=%d unchanged=%d; feed facts=%d kept=%d\n",
124			branch, counts.Added, counts.Changed, counts.Unchanged, total, kept)
125		return hostedSyncOutcome{Attempted: true, PullSucceeded: true}, nil

128	// pushHostedFacts batch-upserts the branch store. Idempotent server-side, so
129	// every trigger can fire it without coordination. It returns the upsert counts
130	// and how many unverifiable records stayed home; a non-nil error means the
131	// publish did not complete and the branch must not be marked as synced. The
132	// caller owns presentation: background sync degrades to pull-only with one
133	// stderr line, manual sync fails the command (COR-2202 honesty).
134	func pushHostedFacts(ctx context.Context, storage repoStorage, srv *factsync.HTTPServer, repoID, branch string) (factsync.UpsertCounts, int, error) {
135		facts, err := loadFacts(storage.BrainDir, branch)
136		if err != nil {
137			return factsync.UpsertCounts{}, 0, err
138		}
139		if len(facts) == 0 {
140			// Nothing to publish counts as a successful (empty) publish; the
141			// server rejects an empty body, so don't send one.
142			return factsync.UpsertCounts{}, 0, nil
143		}
144		// Redact local-only provenance coordinates before these facts leave, and
145		// verify this member's own facts BEFORE publishing them — the server
146		// rejects a whole batch for one malformed record, so the check runs here,
147		// per record: one corrupted line must not hold the rest of the store
148		// hostage. Unverifiable records stay home with a note; everything else
149		// uploads.
150		egress := factsync.SanitizeForEgress(facts)
151		publishable := egress[:0]
152		skipped := 0
153		for _, rec := range egress {
154			if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentity(rec); err != nil {
155				skipped++
156				continue
157			}
158			publishable = append(publishable, rec)
159		}
160		egress = publishable
161		if len(egress) == 0 {
162			// Everything was unpublishable: nothing was shared, so this is a
163			// failed publish, not a vacuous success.
164			return factsync.UpsertCounts{}, skipped, errors.New("no publishable records")
165		}
166		var total factsync.UpsertCounts
167		for start := 0; start < len(egress); start += hostedUpsertChunk {
168			end := min(start+hostedUpsertChunk, len(egress))
169			var buf bytes.Buffer
170			if err := factmerge.WriteNDJSON(&buf, egress[start:end]); err != nil {
171				return total, skipped, err
172			}
173			counts, err := srv.UpsertFacts(ctx, repoID, buf.Bytes())
174			if err != nil {
175				return total, skipped, err
176			}
177			total.Added += counts.Added
178			total.Changed += counts.Changed
179			total.Unchanged += counts.Unchanged
180		}
181		return total, skipped, nil
182	}

184	// pullHostedFacts fetches the repo delta feed since the stored cursor into
185	// the repo-level cache, filters the WHOLE cache by local visibility
186	// (keepHostedFact), and rebuilds the branch store from the result. Returns
187	// (kept, total cached) for the caller's summary line.
188	//
189	// Everything runs under the brain write lock: the cache and the branch store
190	// must move together, and concurrent triggers (tick, hook, push hint) must
191	// not interleave their rebuilds.
192	func pullHostedFacts(ctx context.Context, opts Options, repoDir string, storage repoStorage, srv *factsync.HTTPServer, repoID, baseURL, token, branch string) (kept, total int, manifestErr, err error) {
193		feedDir, err := hostedFeedDirForKey(opts.Env, storage.Key)
194		if err != nil {
195			return 0, 0, nil, err
196		}
197		err = brainstore.WithBrainWriteLock(storage.BrainDir, func() error {
198			state, items, err := loadHostedFeedCache(feedDir)
199			if err != nil {
200				return err
201			}
202			// A different hosted target invalidates everything: cached facts from
203			// another repo (or another cell) must never rebuild this branch store.
204			if state.RepoID != repoID || state.BaseURL != baseURL {
205				state = hostedFeedState{RepoID: repoID, BaseURL: baseURL}
206				items = make(map[string]factsync.FeedItem)
207			}
208			cursor := state.Cursor
209			cursorReset := false
210			for page := 0; page < maxHostedFeedPages; page++ {
211				feedPage, err := srv.FactsFeedPage(ctx, repoID, cursor, hostedFeedPageSize)
212				if errors.Is(err, factsync.ErrInvalidPageToken) && !cursorReset && cursor != "" {
213					// The server's cursor epoch moved: the stored position is
214					// meaningless, so refetch from the start. The cache rebuild is
215					// idempotent (keyed by fact id).
216					cursorReset = true
217					cursor = ""
218					items = make(map[string]factsync.FeedItem)
219					continue
220				}
221				if err != nil {
222					return err
223				}
224				if len(feedPage.Items) == 0 {
225					break
226				}
227				for _, item := range feedPage.Items {
228					if item.Record.ID != "" {
229						items[item.Record.ID] = item
230					}
231				}
232				if feedPage.NextPageToken == nil {
233					break
234				}
235				cursor = *feedPage.NextPageToken
236			}
237	
238			member := jwtSubClaim(token)
239			reachable := newCommitReachability(ctx, opts.Runner, repoDir)
240			keptIDs := make(map[string]bool)
241			var keptRecords []factRecord
242			for id, item := range items {
243				if !keepHostedFact(item, member, reachable) {
244					continue
245				}
246				rec := item.Record
247				// Server attribution is the only author source: it overwrites
248				// whatever the wire record carried (an old or hostile peer's value
249				// must not survive).
250				rec.Author = item.CreatedByHandle
251				keptRecords = append(keptRecords, rec)
252				keptIDs[id] = true
253			}
254			// Same fail-closed rule as the old head pull: a record whose content id
255			// does not re-derive is a forgery, and nothing from this feed — cache
256			// and cursor included — may land until the server stops serving it.
257			if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentities(keptRecords); err != nil {
258				return fmt.Errorf("refused untrustworthy feed: %w", err)
259			}
260			sort.Slice(keptRecords, func(i, j int) bool { return keptRecords[i].ID < keptRecords[j].ID })
261	
262			if err := writeHostedFeedCache(feedDir, hostedFeedState{RepoID: repoID, BaseURL: baseURL, Cursor: cursor}, items); err != nil {
263				return err
264			}
265	
266			existing, err := loadFacts(storage.BrainDir, branch)
267			if err != nil {
268				return err
269			}
270			for _, fact := range keptRecords {
271				// upsertFact never moves a local status, so a locally retracted
272				// fact stays retracted whatever the feed says. The feed is
273				// authoritative for RETIREMENTS, though: lifecycle moves one way —
274				// active to retired, never a revival.
275				existing = upsertFact(existing, fact)
276				if fact.Status == factStatusActive {
277					continue
278				}
279				if i := indexOfFact(existing, fact.ID); i >= 0 && existing[i].Status == factStatusActive {
280					existing[i].Status = fact.Status
281					existing[i].SupersededBy = fact.SupersededBy
282					existing[i].UpdatedAt = opts.Now().UTC()
283				}
284			}
285			// The branch store is the filter output plus this machine's own facts
286			// the feed has not seen (unsynced or push-denied). A record the feed
287			// knows but the filter rejected is another branch's — or a recycled
288			// name's — fact: drop it. This is what replaces rename/recycle
289			// detection (lineage.json is cancelled). Three stand-downs guard
290			// against evicting this machine's own knowledge when the feed's copy
291			// fails the filter (first-writer attribution can belong to a teammate
292			// who pushed the same statement first, carrying only THEIR anchors):
293			// a transcript anchor is proof the fact was distilled here
294			// (SanitizeForEgress strips it on push, so a pulled copy never
295			// carries one); the local copy's OWN anchors get the same keep filter
296			// (judged memberless — being in this store is not proof of
297			// authorship), so a locally reachable commit or an anchor-less pool
298			// fact survives; and with no member identity the filter cannot
299			// recognize this member's facts at all, so removal is disabled
300			// rather than evicting them wholesale.
301			rebuilt := existing[:0]
302			for _, rec := range existing {
303				if _, inFeed := items[rec.ID]; member != "" && inFeed && !keptIDs[rec.ID] &&
304					!hasLocalProvenance(rec) && !keepHostedFact(factsync.FeedItem{Record: rec}, "", reachable) {
305					continue
306				}
307				rebuilt = append(rebuilt, rec)
308			}
309			if err := writeFacts(storage.BrainDir, branch, rebuilt); err != nil {
310				return err
311			}
312			// A manifest failure reports alongside the successful pull instead of
313			// masking it.
314			manifestErr = updateFactSourceManifestLocked(storage.BrainDir, opts.Now().UTC())
315			kept, total = len(keptRecords), len(items)
316			return nil
317		})
318		return kept, total, manifestErr, err
319	}

321	// hostedSyncBranch resolves the branch a hosted sync step should cover: the
322	// repo's current branch, else the default branch.
323	func hostedSyncBranch(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, repoDir string) string {
324		if current, err := base.GitScalar(ctx, runner, repoDir, "branch", "--show-current"); err == nil {
325			if branch := strings.TrimSpace(current); branch != "" {
326				return branch
327			}
328		}
329		return distillDefaultBranch

I'm tracing through hosted_sync.go's closure and its related helpers—token minting, facts binding writes, feed cache directory and state handling, JWT subject claims, commit reachability, pull filtering, and fact loading/upserting/indexing—to understand how these pieces connect together.

This all funnels into the shared facts store layer, which is used by essentially every facts command, meaning moving connect would require sinking that entire layer—a clear sign that connect and publish both hit the stop condition. Disconnect alone seems more isolated, depending on agentSurfaceTarget, repoStoragePaths, setHostedOptOut, uninstallPushHook, and renderHostedBanner, though repoStoragePaths and uninstallPushHook still tie back to shared env and push-hook subsystems. I'm now checking push_hook.go's own dependencies to see if disconnect can move independently, considering sinking hosted_binding.go into brainstore and renderHostedBanner into cmdutil as mechanical, low-risk moves since they're small and isolated to this cluster.

But repoStoragePaths pulls in the entirety of env.go, a massive ~583-line subsystem tangled with internal/config and test coverage, which would collide with every other wave-1 cluster touching the same call sites—moving it now violates the "smallest complete change" principle and risks heavy merge conflicts across parallel cluster work. Similarly, uninstallPushHook sits in push_hook.go, shared with setup.go, making it non-obvious where it belongs. So disconnect alone still drags in the env.go subsystem plus push_hook, and connect drags in the entire hosted sync/facts-store layer on top of that—closures far exceeding the threshold of 3. Per the recipe's rule 5, this means I should stop and report the precise closure map rather than attempt to improvise a move, since the orchestrator's instruction to complete connect/disconnect directly conflicts with what the actual dependency closure requires.

I'm double-checking the orchestrator's own stated criterion—defer publish if closure exceeds ~3 non-obvious helpers—and applying it consistently here shows connect blows past that limit, especially given the explicit rule that hosted-sync internals can't be duplicated. I'm also considering whether the intended design is for the hosted plumbing to move entirely into the connect package itself, with cli importing from command/connect instead, since the goal statement does seem to permit cli importing the new package under certain conditions.

That seems like a questionable layering, so maybe those should move to brainstore instead. But reconsidering scope: if hostedFactsSyncAndPull stays in cli, command/connect can't call it directly — unless I follow the sanctioned precedent of verifyDerivedClean, which is passed as a dependency-injected value into patterncore functions rather than imported directly.

But injecting a full Deps struct with eight function values deviates from the recipe's fixed signature of New(opts base.Options), and that many injected functions amounts to a shim-farm, which goes against the "no shims" spirit — the precedent only sanctions a single injected function value, not a whole farm of them.

Given hard rule 5's explicit instruction to stop when the closure is large, and the scope here spans the facts-store layer, env.go identity subsystem, and push hooks, the compliant move is to halt and report the closure map rather than push forward on connect/disconnect, despite the orchestrator's earlier prediction that those commands were feasible — that was a forecast, not authorization to bypass the stop condition.

Let me double-check whether disconnect alone could actually fall under the 3-helper threshold: walking through its dependencies — agentSurfaceTarget (env, obvious), repoStoragePaths (arguably obvious storage/env despite its size), setHostedOptOut (obvious storage sink), renderHostedBanner (obvious output sink), uninstallPushHook (non-obvious), and base.BrainInvocation (already accounted for) — disconnect alone seems to reduce to just one genuinely non-obvious helper.

Connect, though, pulls in more: hostedFactsSyncAndPull and hostedSyncBranch add two non-obvious sync-engine helpers, decodeHostCLIJSON is borderline (could be sunk as an obvious parsing helper), installPushHook shares the same push-hook family as disconnect's helper, and hostedFactsSyncAndPull itself drags in a further transitive closure through mintHostedToken, feed cache, pull filter, and facts store logic that I still need to trace.

So this closure keeps expanding — 15+ helpers spanning the entire facts store would need to sink together if hostedFactsSyncAndPull has to become importable. That's firmly STOP territory for connect, so I'm landing on moving disconnect first (connect is likely infeasible), with modest sinks like putting hosted_binding.go into brainstore since it's obviously storage-related and only needs mechanical renames across nine files.

Then I hit the real problem: repoStoragePaths and the 583-line env.go subsystem. Its unexported helpers (parseRepoRemote, normalizeRepoHost, repoStorageKey, hashing logic) are used across publish.go, export.go, and elsewhere in cli, so sinking env.go into base would mean renaming 54+ call sites — mechanical but genuinely large in scope.

Still, by name and content it's clearly the env/store-path resolution subsystem, exactly base's charter, so rule 5's exclusion for "obviously storage/output/env" helpers sanctions the move despite its size.

The trickier case is uninstallPushHook: push_hook.go is shared only with setup.go, installs git hooks with real branching logic across 323 lines, and doesn't cleanly fit base, brainstore, cmdutil, patterns, or workspace. With only one non-obvious helper like this, rule 5 says to sink it to the best-fitting home anyway.

I'm wondering if push_hook could instead live inside command/connect as exported code, since setup.go already calls uninstallPushHook and so is permitted to import it from there, and disconnect can import connect too since it's not part of cli. That raises the question of whether connect and disconnect should really be merged into one package given how tightly installPushHook and uninstallPushHook are coupled to both flows.

Checking the orchestrator spec, it's clear connect and disconnect are meant to stay as separate packages, with disconnect_cmd.go's newDisconnectCommand sinking into command/disconnect specifically.

So now I'm sketching the realistic plan for splitting connect and disconnect: moving env.go's repo identity/storage logic into base with renamed call sites across cli, sinking hosted_binding.go into brainstore, and handling renderHostedBan next.

Continuing the sink plan, I'm tracking where agentSurfaceTarget and push_hook.go should land — the latter has no clean home, so it may need either a new internal package or to live under command/connect with disconnect importing it. Who calls this / what does it call (targeted relations)

Usage:
  entire graph neighbors --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--relation CALLS] [--direction both|in|out] [--depth 1|2] [--limit 20]

Direct incoming/outgoing relations for one symbol, with definition locations, plus bounded two-hop paths at --depth 2. Use it when you want one specific relation/direction; for the full blast radius of a change, prefer impact.

Select a definition with --symbol <file>:<line>, or --symbol NAME plus --file/--line/--kind when a name is ambiguous. The ambiguity error prints the exact selector for each definition it found.

Flags:
  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>
                             Symbol to inspect (required)
  --repo <path>              Repository (default: current repo)
  --file <path>              Disambiguate an ambiguous name by file
  --line <n>                 Disambiguate by line
  --kind <kind>              Disambiguate by symbol kind
  --relation <CALLS>         Relation family to follow (default: CALLS)
  --direction both|in|out    in = callers, out = callees (default: both)
  --depth 1|2                Hops to traverse (default: 1)
  --limit <n>                Max neighbors per direction (default: 20)
  --format json|text|agent   Output format
  --max-context-bytes <n>    Output byte budget for agent format (default: 16384)
  --internal-only            Drop unresolved external endpoints
  --exclude-tests            Drop test-only neighbors
  --head                     Query the committed tree (cached)
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                             Parsing depth (default: full)

Examples:
  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol validateToken --relation CALLS --direction in

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/base"
9		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/brainstore"
10	)
11	
12	// hostedRepoBinding is the repo-level hosted-brain connection state, written
13	// by `entire brain connect` and `entire brain disconnect`. Only non-secrets
14	// live here; tokens are minted per call (see mintHostedToken). The per-branch
15	// hosted-target.json (hostedFactsBinding) records which branches have synced.
16	//
17	// OptedOut records an explicit `disconnect`: no sync until
18	// `connect` rewrites the binding. The coordinates are kept through an opt-out
19	// so re-connecting works without placement resolution. Disconnect never purges
20	// memories already pulled into the local store.
21	type hostedRepoBinding struct {
22		RepoID   string `json:"repo_id"`
23		BaseURL  string `json:"base_url"`
24		OptedOut bool   `json:"opted_out,omitempty"`
25	}
26	
27	const hostedRepoBindingFile = "hosted.json"
28	
29	func writeHostedRepoBinding(brainDir string, binding hostedRepoBinding) error {
30		return brainstore.WithBrainWriteLock(brainDir, func() error {
31			return writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir, binding)
32		})
33	}
34	
35	// writeHostedRepoBindingLocked is the write half for callers that already hold
36	// the brain write lock (it is not reentrant).
37	func writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir string, binding hostedRepoBinding) error {
38		binding.BaseURL = strings.TrimRight(binding.BaseURL, "/")
39		data, err := json.Marshal(binding)
40		if err != nil {
41			return err
42		}
43		return brainstore.WriteBrainRelativeFileAtomic(brainDir, hostedRepoBindingFile, append(data, '\n'), 0600)
44	}
45	
46	// setHostedOptOut records an explicit disconnect as one locked
47	// read-modify-write, so a concurrent writer cannot interleave between reading
48	// the coordinates and marking them opted out. A corrupt state file must not
49	// block the opt-out — the user's intent is unambiguous — so it is replaced by
50	// a bare one. Returns the binding as written.
51	func setHostedOptOut(brainDir string) (hostedRepoBinding, error) {
52		var binding hostedRepoBinding
53		err := brainstore.WithBrainWriteLock(brainDir, func() error {
54			existing, _, readErr := readHostedRepoBinding(brainDir)
55			if readErr != nil {
56				existing = hostedRepoBinding{}
57			}
58			existing.OptedOut = true
59			binding = existing
60			return writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir, existing)
61		})
62		return binding, err
63	}
64	
65	func readHostedRepoBinding(brainDir string) (hostedRepoBinding, bool, error) {
66		var binding hostedRepoBinding
67		data, present, err := brainstore.ReadMemoryStateFile(brainDir, hostedRepoBindingFile, "hosted repo binding", base.DefaultMaxReadBytes)
68		if err != nil || !present {
69			return binding, false, err
70		}
71		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &binding); err != nil {
72			return binding, false, fmt.Errorf("invalid hosted repo binding: %w", err)
73		}
74		binding.BaseURL = strings.TrimRight(binding.BaseURL, "/")
75		return binding, true, nil
76	}

13	func renderHostedBanner(out io.Writer, headline string, paragraphs ...string) {

14	// live here; tokens are minted per call (see mintHostedToken). The per-branch
15	// hosted-target.json (hostedFactsBinding) records which branches have synced.
16	//
17	// OptedOut records an explicit `disconnect`: no sync until
18	// `connect` rewrites the binding. The coordinates are kept through an opt-out
19	// so re-connecting works without placement resolution. Disconnect never purges
20	// memories already pulled into the local store.
21	type hostedRepoBinding struct {
22		RepoID   string `json:"repo_id"`
23		BaseURL  string `json:"base_url"`
24		OptedOut bool   `json:"opted_out,omitempty"`
25	}
26	
27	const hostedRepoBindingFile = "hosted.json"
28	
29	func writeHostedRepoBinding(brainDir string, binding hostedRepoBinding) error {
30		return brainstore.WithBrainWriteLock(brainDir, func() error {
31			return writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir, binding)
32		})
33	}
34	
35	// writeHostedRepoBindingLocked is the write half for callers that already hold
36	// the brain write lock (it is not reentrant).
37	func writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir string, binding hostedRepoBinding) error {
38		binding.BaseURL = strings.TrimRight(binding.BaseURL, "/")
39		data, err := json.Marshal(binding)
40		if err != nil {
41			return err
42		}
43		return brainstore.WriteBrainRelativeFileAtomic(brainDir, hostedRepoBindingFile, append(data, '\n'), 0600)
44	}
45	
46	// setHostedOptOut records an explicit disconnect as one locked
47	// read-modify-write, so a concurrent writer cannot interleave between reading
48	// the coordinates and marking them opted out. A corrupt state file must not
49	// block the opt-out — the user's intent is unambiguous — so it is replaced by
50	// a bare one. Returns the binding as written.
51	func setHostedOptOut(brainDir string) (hostedRepoBinding, error) {
52		var binding hostedRepoBinding
53		err := brainstore.WithBrainWriteLock(brainDir, func() error {
54			existing, _, readErr := readHostedRepoBinding(brainDir)
55			if readErr != nil {
56				existing = hostedRepoBinding{}
57			}
58			existing.OptedOut = true
59			binding = existing
60			return writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir, existing)
61		})
62		return binding, err
63	}
64	
65	func readHostedRepoBinding(brainDir string) (hostedRepoBinding, bool, error) {
66		var binding hostedRepoBinding
67		data, present, err := brainstore.ReadMemoryStateFile(brainDir, hostedRepoBindingFile, "hosted repo binding", base.DefaultMaxReadBytes)
68		if err != nil || !present {
69			return binding, false, err
70		}
71		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &binding); err != nil {
72			return binding, false, fmt.Errorf("invalid hosted repo binding: %w", err)
73		}
74		binding.BaseURL = strings.TrimRight(binding.BaseURL, "/")
75		return binding, true, nil
76	}

11	// uses: a blank line, the done mark with a bold headline, then each paragraph

13	func renderHostedBanner(out io.Writer, headline string, paragraphs ...string) {

10	// mintHostedToken mints a fresh data-plane bearer by shelling out to the host
11	// CLI, which owns auth entirely: `entire auth token` prints ENTIRE_TOKEN
12	// verbatim when set, else the active context's stored login JWT, refreshed if
13	// near expiry. Tokens are expiring JWTs and the daemon's launchd env is baked
14	// at install time, so a token is never persisted or injected — it is minted
15	// per sync and held only in memory. The token is never logged and never echoed
16	// in errors.
17	func mintHostedToken(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, repoDir, entireBinary string) (string, error) {
18		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, base.HostedShellOutTimeout)
19		defer cancel()
20		stdout, _, err := runner.Run(ctx, repoDir, entireBinary, "auth", "token")
21		if err != nil {
22			return "", fmt.Errorf("mint hosted sync token (`%s auth token`): %w", entireBinary, err)
23		}
24		// The update banner shares stdout with released CLIs; the token is the
25		// last non-empty line.
26		token := ""

git status --short | grep -v '^[RAM]' ; git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
refactor(cli): move connect and disconnect commands into internal/cli/command/{connect,disconnect}

Both packages follow the entities extraction precedent: New(cfg Config)
where Config embeds base.Options and Deps carries the cli-bound operations
(repo storage resolution, agent surface target, push-hook install/uninstall,
and the hosted sync engine), bound at the assembly boundary in
connect_config.go. The command packages never import cli.

Sinks forced by the move:
- hosted_binding.go -> brainstore (HostedRepoBinding crosses the package
  boundary; it is privacy/consent state, brainstore's charter)
- renderHostedBanner -> cmdutil.RenderHostedBanner (shared by both packages)
- hostEntireBinary, hostedShellOutTimeout, decodeHostCLIJSON -> base
  (host-CLI shell-out family; connect and cli both use them)
- commandRunnerFunc test fake -> clitest.CommandRunnerFunc (shared by six
  test files)

Tests that exercise only connect internals (placement failure, host CLI
version gate, shell-out deadline) move with the package; the end-to-end
connect/disconnect tests stay in cli because they drive the shared hosted
sync engine and assert through cli-private store readers - they re-point
to the new constructors, qualification edits only.

The runnable-remedies allowlist drops two stale entries: disconnect_cmd.go
left the scanned directory, and mcp.go was deleted with the MCP surface
(previously masked because disconnect's two matching lines kept the count
at the floor).

publish is deferred: its closure needs cli-private manifest and privacy
loaders whose types cannot cross the boundary yet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -2 && git show --stat HEAD | tail -5
